why_how.text: Before entering a highway, avoid mistaking the exit ramp for the entrance; watch ONE WAY, WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs.
A green HIGHWAY ENTRANCE sign may identify an entrance ramp, but is not always present.
A white edge line on the right and yellow on the left indicate the proper direction of travel on the ramp.
In a shared weaving lane, an entering driver yields to the exiting driver.
Use an acceleration lane to build toward traffic speed, checking the side mirror and looking over the shoulder for a gap.
Move into the exit lane early and slow only after entering that lane.
If the exit is missed, use the next exit rather than stopping, reversing, crossing multiple lanes suddenly or crossing the median.
Exit-ramp warning signs indicate the maximum safe ramp speed.
At sixty-five miles per hour, a vehicle covers almost one hundred feet per second.
When passing on a highway, change only one lane at a time and signal each lane change well ahead.
A through driver may help a highway entrant by changing lanes courteously, but must first verify space is clear.
Highway hypnosis develops when prolonged staring replaces scanning ahead, behind and around the vehicle.
Along a curb, park as close as possible and no farther than twelve inches away.
